अगु अ-गु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. गो with अ), Ved. desti-
tute of cows, or of rays; poor; destitute of hymns,
wicked; (उस्), m., N. of Rāhu or the ascending node.

अगुण अ-गुण, अस्, आ, अम्, destitute of qua-
lities or attributes (sometimes said of the supreme
being); destitute of good qualities; (अस्), m. a fault.
—अगुण-ता, f. absence of good qualities.
—अगु-
ण-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, destitute of qualities, especially
of good qualities.
—अगुण-वादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, fault-
finding, censorious.
—अगुण-शील, अस्, आ, अम्, of a
worthless character.

अगुप्त अ-गुप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, unhidden, uncon-
cealed; unprotected; not keeping a secret.

अगुरु अ-गुरु, उस्, ऊ or वी, उ, not heavy,
light; (in prosody) short as a short vowel alone or
before a single consonant; (उस्, उ), m. n. the fragrant
Aloe wood and tree, Aquiluria Agallocha; the Śiśu
tree; the tree which yields Bdellium, Amyris Agallocha.
—अगुरु-शिंशपा, f. the Śiśu tree, (probably distinct
words, शिंशपा being added to explain अगुरु.)

अगूढ अ-गूढ, अस्, आ, अम्, unconcealed,
manifest.
—अगूढ-गन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, having an
unconcealed smell; (अम्), n. Asa Fœtida.
—अगूढ-
भाव, अस्, आ, अम्, having a transparent disposition.

आगुर् 1. आ-गुर्, cl. 6. A. -गुरते, -रितुम्
(गुर् = rt. गॄ, see आ-गॄ), to approve, to agree or
assent to, to promise, to pronounce the Āgur.

2. आ-गुर्, ऊर्, f., Ved., N. of a class of plauditory or
approving exclamations or formularies used by the
priests in sacrificial rites; assent, an agreement.

आ-गुरण or आ-गूरण or आ-गूर्ण, अम्, n. recita-
tion of the Āgur.

आ-गूर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. performing or pronounc-
ing the Āgur.

आगुरव आगुरव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. अ-गुरु),
originating from or formed of Agallochum. See
अ-गुरु.
